description:
Review finding from PR #121 / bedrock-qzr.18.

Established behavior

`TransactionStreams.read_previous_version/1` distinguishes unsupported or invalid WAL bytes from POSIX failures returned by `File.open/2` and `:file.pread/3`. `Segment.from_path/1` discards that distinction: every error except `:unsupported_wal_format` is returned as `{:invalid_wal_format, path}`.

As a result, resource failures such as `:emfile`, `:enfile`, or `:enomem` while opening or reading a segment header bypass Shale Server retry handling and are raised as an invalid recovery cursor. Other I/O failures such as permissions or device errors are also mislabeled as format corruption.

Cold-start acquisition is also not transactional. `do_initialization/1` starts a linked SegmentRecycler before calling `load_or_create_segments/2`, even though the recycler argument is unused by segment loading. If directory listing returns a retryable resource error, the server remains alive for backoff but the newly started recycler is neither stored in State nor stopped. A subsequent attempt starts another recycler.

This is an availability, diagnostics, and resource-ownership defect. There is no evidence that it causes Shale to accept corrupt WAL data.

Required direction

- Preserve format and I/O failures as distinct domain errors carrying the segment path, for example `{:wal_format, path, reason}` and `{:wal_io, path, posix_reason}`.
- Eliminate the `File.exists?/1` precheck and classify the result of the actual open/read operation, avoiding a check-then-open race.
- Apply retry policy once at the Server initialization boundary. Retry explicitly transient resource failures; fail closed with an accurate cause for unsupported/invalid WALs and non-retryable I/O failures.
- Load and validate the existing WAL set before starting the recycler, or otherwise guarantee cleanup of every staged resource before returning a retry/error result.
- Treat recycler and Demux acquisition as owned initialization resources: a failed attempt must either publish them in State on success or synchronously tear them down.

Acceptance criteria

- Header open and pread errors retain their POSIX cause and segment path through TransactionStreams, Segment, ColdStarting, and Server.
- Legacy or malformed bytes remain format errors and continue to fail closed without being retried as resource exhaustion.
- `:emfile`, `:enfile`, and `:enomem` from directory listing, header open, or header read enter the bounded exponential-backoff path.
- Non-retryable I/O failures are reported as WAL I/O failures, not format corruption.
- A deterministic test injects a transient header-read resource error, observes a retry, removes the fault, and verifies successful initialization.
- Tests prove each failed attempt leaves no unowned SegmentRecycler or Demux process and that only one live instance of each is published after success.
- The existing maximum-attempt and delay behavior remains bounded and testable.
- No retry path mutates, recycles, truncates, or rewrites an existing WAL segment.
title: Make Shale WAL cold start transactional and preserve I/O errors
